passage:
I still remember how Keerthana began the meeting: "I'm going to be direct, because you deserve that." She told me the division was being cut and my role was included. She didn't hide behind policy words, and she looked at me the whole time.

Then she said she had argued with senior management for a longer notice period and better severance, and won part of it. She offered to write my reference that same afternoon and to introduce me to a contact at a logistics firm.

I was angry with the company and, strangely, grateful to her. My first reflex was to say "You don't have to," but I stopped myself and said, "Thank you. It matters."

We still message every few months. Last week she sent me a job link. I'm Ayesha, and I'll return that kindness one day.

qa.q: What did Keerthana offer Ayesha besides news of the cut?
qa.a: Keerthana offered to write a reference that afternoon and to introduce Ayesha to a contact at a logistics firm, after arguing for better severance.

qa.q: What was Ayesha feeling towards Keerthana during the meeting?
qa.a: Ayesha was angry with the company but grateful to Keerthana, whose direct and honest manner felt like care.

qa.q: Why was it wise for Ayesha to accept the help and stay in touch?
qa.a: Accepting the reference and thanking Keerthana honoured the effort made for Ayesha, and the connection has already produced a job link.

qa.q: What was it probably like for Keerthana to deliver the news?
qa.a: Keerthana likely found it hard, since she chose to be direct and to fight for severance while carrying out a decision she did not make alone.

grounding: Ayesha is laid off by a manager who is honest, offers a reference and fights for severance; she accepts help and stays in touch.

passage:
The sugar factory office near Kolhapur was closing its accounts section, and Kalyani, the section head, called Tejas in herself instead of letting the head office send a letter.
"I'm not going to wrap this up nicely. Your post goes at the end of March," she said. "I argued for three months' pay instead of one, and they agreed. And I'll write you a reference that says exactly how good you are."
Tejas stared at the calendar on the wall. His throat felt tight. Then he noticed the dark circles under her eyes.
"You fought for that?"
"For all six of you."
He swallowed. "Thank you, madam. Truly."
Before he left in March, he gave her a box of pedhas from his mother's kitchen and saved her number. In June, Kalyani phoned: a friend at a dairy in Sangli needed an accountant.

qa.q: How much pay did Kalyani argue for?
qa.a: Three months' pay instead of one.

qa.q: What was Tejas feeling as he stared at the calendar?
qa.a: He felt shocked and sad, his throat tight at losing his post.

qa.q: How did Tejas accept Kalyani's help well?
qa.a: He thanked her sincerely, gave her a gift, and kept in touch, which later led to a job lead in Sangli.

qa.q: How might Kalyani feel delivering the news herself?
qa.a: Kalyani is probably tired and sad, with dark circles under her eyes, yet caring enough to tell each person honestly and fight for them.

grounding: A manager delivers layoff news honestly, fights for better terms and offers a reference; the protagonist accepts, thanks her and stays in touch.

passage:
Tomas ran the Porto branch of the bookshop chain, and on a grey Tuesday he asked Sofia to stay after closing. He made two coffees and didn't sit behind the counter.
"Head office is closing this branch in May. I found out on Friday, and I wanted you to hear it from me first." He slid a paper across. "I've written you a reference. And I've asked them for an extra month's pay for everyone. They haven't said yes yet, but I'm pushing."
Sofia's eyes filled. She loved this shop, its creaky stairs and the poetry corner she'd rebuilt.
"Why are you doing all this?"
"Because you'd do it for me."
She wiped her eyes and read the reference twice. "Thank you. I mean it."
"Stay in touch. I know people in the Lisbon shops."
In July, a message came from him: "A friend at a publisher needs someone like you."

qa.q: When is the Porto branch closing?
What was Sofia feeling when Tomas told her the news?
qa.a: She felt sad and heartbroken about losing the shop she loved, yet grateful for how he told her.

qa.q: What did Sofia do that kept the door open for the future?
qa.a: She thanked Tomas sincerely, accepted the reference, and stayed in touch, which led to a lead at a publisher in July.

qa.q: How might Tomas see the moment when Sofia asks why he is doing all this?
qa.a: Tomas seems to feel it is simply fair and caring, since he trusts she would do the same for him.

grounding: A manager delivers the news honestly, offers a reference and fights for severance; the protagonist accepts, thanks him and stays in touch.
